newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close down 3.52 percent at 8,187.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close down 3.52 percent at 8,187.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply lower on Friday following across-the-board selling by investors who feared that many of the shares were overvalued, brokers said.
The weighted index tumbled by 298.66 points or 3.52 percent to finish at 8,187.
Turnover was an active T$121.6 billion.

Despite a newspaper report that the 386 listed firms' combined net profit in the first quarter surged a year-on-year 43 percent to T$70.62 billion, brokers said many firms' share prices were overvalued.
Sentiment was further dampened by the government's apparent attempt to cool the market, brokers said.

The central bank had continued to issue negotiable certificates of deposit to tighten banking system liquidity in recent sessions. The bank has confirmed that it was responding to the liquidity situation but denied that it was motivated by the recent stock rally.
"The government's attitude is not very supportive at the moment and many investors have been driven to the sidelines," said Oliver Fang, an analyst of National Securities.
Amy Huang, analyst at Nomura Securities, said a general lack of confidence in the market's upward potential had triggered Friday's heavy losses.
"I did not hear any particular negative news to trigger today's selling," she said. "It's probably because of a lack of confidence."
Worries over deteriorating social order and a possible change in the central bank's monetary policy also dampened buyers' enthusiasm, brokers said.
The central bank is slated to hold a board meeting on May 8.
